decisions.statement: A service wanting no deploy is chosen by nothing here.
A service with a deploy running is passed over rather than waited on.
A service inside the cooldown its page states is passed over.
The cooldown is counted from the moment that service's last deploy ended.
A service whose last deploy ended at no moment is past its cooldown.
A service any service it depends on wants a deploy for is held back.
Holding back that way carries down a chain, since a service held back wants a deploy still.
A service naming a service that is nowhere is held back by nothing.
The one chosen is the able service whose deployed commit is oldest.
A service never deployed is older than every service that has been.
Two services equally far behind are ordered by slug, so a tick is repeatable.
A tick with nothing able to deploy chooses nothing rather than refusing.
Nothing here works out whether a commit changed what a service is built from.
Nothing here puts anything up, and nothing here reads a page.
A ring of services depending on each other is chosen from by nothing here.
Whether a service wants a deploy is a question asked here rather than a fact handed in.
That question is put in order, furthest behind first, and stops at the one chosen.
A service whose last deploy refused waits longer than its own cooldown before being chosen.
That wait is what keeps a service that cannot be put up from starving the rest of its kind.

definition: which service a deploy loop puts up next, out of the services wanting a deploy
